result.summary: Exposes the node's `interfaces::Chain` over IPC using Cap'n Proto proxy wrappers, split into a stable `Chain` interface and an `UnstableChain` interface. The stable interface covers basic block lookups for external clients under Cap'n Proto backward-compatibility rules, while `UnstableChain` exposes the remaining methods for internal Bitcoin Core consumers. It also updates the `src/ipc/libmultiprocess` subtree and makes minor adjustments to `interfaces::Chain` method signatures to support code generation.
result.problem: Processes connecting to `bitcoin-node` over IPC via `-ipcbind` cannot read chain data or follow chain notifications, blocking multiprocess wallet separation (#10102). Exposing the entire raw `interfaces::Chain` C++ interface to external IPC clients would freeze internal wallet APIs against future refactoring.
evidence: PR description: 'Processes connected to bitcoin-node over IPC (with -ipcbind) can use the Mining interface, but they can't currently use the Chain interface read chain data or follow chain events. Chain data could be useful to third-party clients and Bitcoin Core's own wallet could use this as well to run in a separate process (#10102).'
PR description references #34981 ('multiprocess: expose existing interfaces or design new ones?') as the rationale for splitting into stable and unstable interfaces.
result.scope_notes: Carries an update to the src/ipc/libmultiprocess subtree accounting for the majority of changed files and commits, alongside new Cap'n Proto schema and wrapper files. Also includes minor signature adjustments in src/interfaces/chain.h (removing const qualification from two estimation methods and passing updateRwSetting callbacks by value).
result.changed_since_previous: The bundled libmultiprocess subtree update was refreshed with upstream changes including v14 platform support and CI updates, and a compiler flag was added to suppress -Wc++23-lambda-attributes warnings.
result.card: Exposes the Chain interface over IPC using Cap'n Proto, splitting it into a version-stable Chain interface with basic block lookup methods and an UnstableChain interface for Bitcoin Core internal consumers. Currently, chain data and notifications are inaccessible over IPC, blocking multiprocess wallet separation (#10102) and external clients connecting via -ipcbind. This is a core prerequisite for running the wallet in an isolated process (#19460) and depends on #36520.

risk.why: Bugs in Cap'n Proto serialization or proxy wrappers could cause node crashes or memory errors when IPC requests are processed, though IPC is only enabled when configured via -ipcbind.
